boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Saint Anselm College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food stops in Manchester, including campus dining, with late availability documented by direct official sources.

cards.title: Coffee Shop and Pub
cards.subtitle: Behind Alumni Hall, Saint Anselm College
cards.notes: Use the Coffee Shop’s made-to-order menu for an on-campus evening meal; consult Dining Services for the current operating schedule.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus food stop with pizza, calzones, sandwiches, ice cream, and milkshakes.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm states that the Coffee Shop and Pub are open throughout the day and night, and lists made-to-order food and ice cream offerings.
cards.source_title: Coffee Shop and Pub | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Official college page says the venue is open throughout the day and night; operating schedules may change.

cards.title: Pizza 911
cards.subtitle: 108 Webster Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Plan a pickup or delivery order from the Webster Street shop when you need a late food option; verify holiday changes before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A Manchester pizza shop offering takeout and delivery late into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza 911 lists hours until 11:00 PM Sunday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday at 108 Webster Street.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 10:30 AM–11 PM Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 AM–midnight Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Giovanni’s Roast Beef & Pizza
cards.subtitle: 379 South Willow Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Use the South Willow Street shop for a late pickup or delivery meal, particularly on Friday or Saturday; confirm hours before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A pizza and roast-beef restaurant with later Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Giovanni’s lists its Manchester location at 379 South Willow Street and Friday–Saturday hours until 2:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official hours list 10 AM–10 PM Monday–Saturday, with Friday–Saturday shown until 2 AM; Sunday until 9 PM.

cards.title: Alley Cat Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 486 Chestnut Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Call ahead or order online for pizza near downtown; the restaurant’s official hours show the latest availability on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Chestnut Street pizzeria whose official site lists late-week evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Alley Cat Pizzeria lists 486 Chestnut Street in Manchester and hours until 10 PM Monday–Thursday and 11 PM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 11 AM–10 PM Monday–Thursday, 11 AM–11 PM Friday–Saturday, and noon–8 PM Sunday.

cards.title: Zo’s Place
cards.subtitle: 102 Elm Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Choose the Elm Street location for a late Thursday-through-Saturday food stop; use the business’s location page to reconfirm the day’s hours.
cards.short_summary: An Elm Street restaurant with Thursday through Saturday hours extending to 1 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Zo’s Place lists its Manchester location at 102 Elm Street and hours until 1:00 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official Manchester hours: 11 AM–10 PM Monday–Wednesday, 11 AM–1 AM Thursday–Saturday, and noon–10 PM Sunday.

cards.title: Papa Johns Pizza
cards.subtitle: 223 South Willow Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Place a carryout or delivery order from the South Willow Street location when earlier options are closed; check the live location page first.
cards.short_summary: A South Willow Street pizza option with carryout and delivery listed until 1 or 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists carryout and delivery at 223 South Willow Street until 1:00 AM daily and until 2:00 AM Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Pizza, 223 South Willow Street
cards.access_notes: Official carryout and delivery hours are 10 AM–1 AM Sunday–Thursday and 10 AM–2 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers
cards.subtitle: 782 South Willow Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Use the South Willow Street location for a late dine-in, pickup, or drive-thru meal; its official locator lists the same nightly closing time.
cards.short_summary: A chicken-finger restaurant with dine-in and drive-thru service listed until 1 AM daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane’s lists its 782 South Willow Street Manchester restaurant, dine-in, and drive-thru as open until 1:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant, dine-in, and drive-thru hours are 10 AM–1 AM Sunday through Saturday.

cards.title: Wingstop Manchester
cards.subtitle: 581 Second Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Order carryout or delivery from the Second Street location when you need a later meal; review the live location page for any service changes.
cards.short_summary: A Second Street wing restaurant with carryout and delivery listed until 1 AM every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Wingstop lists carryout and delivery at 581 Second Street in Manchester from 10:30 AM to 1:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Official carryout and delivery hours: 10:30 AM–1 AM Sunday through Saturday.

cards.title: Domino’s Pizza
cards.subtitle: 250 Dubuque Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Use the Dubuque Street store’s ordering page for the current evening cutoff and choose pickup or delivery only when the location is accepting orders.
cards.short_summary: A Dubuque Street pizza location whose official page lists availability until 1 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s official location page identifies the Manchester store at 250 Dubuque Street and states it is open until 1:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists the store as open until 1 AM; Domino’s notes that hours vary by location.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 1050 Second Street, Manchester
cards.notes: Use the Second Street restaurant for a late drive-thru, dine-in, or delivery order; check the official locator before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A Second Street Taco Bell whose official locator lists 24-hour drive-thru availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists 1050 Second Street in Manchester as open late, with drive-thru hours shown as 12:00 AM–12:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Official locator lists drive-thru hours of 12 AM–12 AM every day and marks the location Open Late.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces with documented uses for studying, gathering, recreation, reflection, arts, and events.

cards.entity_name: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.title: Jean Student Center
cards.subtitle: Central student hub on campus
cards.notes: Use the central lounge and study areas between commitments, then check the building’s floor maps to locate student-facing offices.
cards.short_summary: A central complex for gathering, services, lounge time, and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The college describes the Jean Student Center as a hub where students gather, work, and learn, with lounge and study areas.
cards.source_title: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; consult the college for current building access and event availability.

cards.title: Jean Student Center Game Room
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.notes: Plan a low-key game break with friends; email the Student Center if you need to reserve the room for a function.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor room for games, music, television, and informal time together.
cards.evidence_claim: The college says the Game Room is a ground-floor place for students to relax, play games, and hang out with friends.
cards.source_title: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.access_notes: Reservation information is available from the Jean Student Center; availability may vary.

cards.title: Multi-Faith Prayer Room
cards.subtitle: Main level, Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.notes: Stop in for quiet reflection or meditation; contact Campus Ministry in advance if your faith-sharing group needs private use.
cards.short_summary: A drop-in reflection space in the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm provides the Multi-Faith Prayer Room for community members to pray, meditate, reflect, and find quiet.
cards.source_title: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.access_notes: Generally drop-in; it may be reserved through Campus Ministry for appropriate private use.

cards.entity_name: Thomas A. Melucci Jr. ’88 Memorial Auditorium
cards.title: Mellucci Memorial Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Jean Student Center, ground and main-level access
cards.notes: Look for lectures, events, and watch parties here; use the Student Center’s reservation contact when planning an eligible gathering.
cards.short_summary: A 250-seat Student Center venue for campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The college identifies this 250-seat theater as home to events, lectures, and watch parties.
cards.source_title: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.access_notes: Event and reservation availability varies; access from the Student Center ground or main level.

cards.title: Geisel Library
cards.subtitle: Campus library and research space
cards.notes: Choose a quiet or group-work setting, reserve a study room through Circulation, and ask the Reference Desk when research gets stuck.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines research help, study spaces, and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Geisel Library offers resources, services, study spaces, research help, and study-room reservations.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are reserved through the Circulation Desk; library access and hours may change.

cards.title: Geisel Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Main level, Geisel Library
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative assignment or technology-heavy project, and use the main-level workspace alongside the IT Help Desk.
cards.short_summary: A remodeled main-level workspace designed for individual and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says its Learning Commons was created to accommodate individual and collaborative study and includes the IT Help Desk.
cards.access_notes: Located in Geisel Library; follow current library access rules and equipment policies.

cards.title: Abbey Church
cards.subtitle: Campus church at Saint Anselm Abbey
cards.notes: Visit respectfully for personal reflection, or consult the Abbey’s schedule before attending Mass or the Liturgy of the Hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus church used for prayer, reflection, and daily monastic worship.
cards.evidence_claim: The college calls the Abbey Church a peaceful place for prayer and reflection and states that Abbey monks hold Mass and Liturgy of the Hours there daily.
cards.access_notes: Worship schedules and access are subject to the Abbey’s current practices.

cards.entity_name: Alva de Mars Megan Chapel Art Center
cards.title: Megan Chapel Art Center
cards.subtitle: Alumni Hall
cards.notes: Check the college’s arts listings before you go, then spend time with the current exhibition in this campus gallery.
cards.short_summary: A named gallery space in Alumni Hall for viewing art.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm’s audio tour identifies the Alva de Mars Megan Chapel Art Center as part of Alumni Hall.
cards.access_notes: Exhibition and gallery access may depend on current programming and building access.

cards.title: Carr Center and Stoutenburgh Gymnasium
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation and athletics complex
cards.notes: Check current recreation access before heading over, whether you are meeting up for courts, fitness, or a scheduled athletic event.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose campus facility for fitness, courts, and athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: The college says the Carr Center and Stoutenburgh Gymnasium include basketball, volleyball, racquetball and tennis courts plus a fitness center.
cards.access_notes: Recreation and event access are subject to current facility schedules and college policies.

cards.title: Goulet Science Center
cards.subtitle: Campus science building
cards.notes: Use the reading room or computer center for coursework when available, and look for department events connected with the sciences.
cards.short_summary: A science building with a reading room, computer center, greenhouse, and specialized labs.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm states that Goulet Science Center includes a reading room, computer center, greenhouse, and science laboratories.
cards.access_notes: Academic rooms and labs may have restricted access; confirm availability with the relevant department.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Geisel Library study environments, from reservable whiteboard rooms to silent carrels and collaborative lower-level seating.

cards.title: Geisel Library Study Room 1
cards.subtitle: Upper Level · group room for up to six
cards.notes: Reserve through the Circulation Desk, bring your student ID for key checkout, and use the whiteboard to map a small-group work session.
cards.short_summary: A six-person upper-level room with a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 1 is on Geisel Library’s upper level, holds up to six people, and has a whiteboard; student reservations are limited to two hours per day.
cards.access_notes: Saint Anselm students only; reserve by calling 603-641-7300 or visiting Circulation. Present student ID to check out the key; two hours per day.

cards.title: Geisel Library Study Room 2
cards.subtitle: Upper Level · group room for up to six
cards.notes: Coordinate a group beforehand, reserve at Circulation, and use the whiteboard for shared outlines, problem sets, or review prompts.
cards.short_summary: A second six-person upper-level room with a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 2 is an upper-level Geisel Library group study room for up to six people and includes a whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Saint Anselm students only; reserve by calling 603-641-7300 or visiting Circulation. Present student ID to check out the key; two hours per day.

cards.title: Geisel Library Study Room 3
cards.subtitle: Upper Level · group room for up to eight
cards.notes: Reserve this room when a shared screen would help; the monitor and whiteboard support comparing drafts, slides, or research materials together.
cards.short_summary: An eight-person group room with a monitor and whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 3 is on Geisel Library’s upper level, holds up to eight people, and includes a flat-screen monitor and whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Saint Anselm students only; reserve by calling 603-641-7300 or visiting Circulation. Present student ID to check out the key; two hours per day.

cards.title: Geisel Library Study Room 4
cards.subtitle: Upper Level · group room for up to eight
cards.notes: Book this upper-level room for a group session that needs a display; check out markers at Circulation or Periodicals for the whiteboard.
cards.short_summary: An eight-person room equipped for shared-screen group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 4 is an upper-level Geisel Library group study room for up to eight people with a flat-screen monitor and whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Saint Anselm students only; reserve by calling 603-641-7300 or visiting Circulation. Present student ID to check out the key; two hours per day.

cards.title: Geisel Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Main Level · tables, armchairs, and windows
cards.notes: Choose a table for spread-out materials or an armchair for reading; quiet talking is allowed on the main level, so plan accordingly.
cards.short_summary: Main-level seating with tables, armchairs, and window light.
cards.evidence_claim: The main-level Reading Room has large group study tables, soft armchairs, windows, and the Leisure Reading collection; quiet talking is allowed on the main level.
cards.access_notes: Located on Geisel Library’s main level. Follow library sound-level and food policies.

cards.title: Geisel Library Reference Area
cards.subtitle: Main Level · lamps and swivel-table armchairs
cards.notes: Set up at a lamped table for sustained work, or use a swivel-table armchair when you need a compact spot for a laptop and notes.
cards.short_summary: A main-level reference area with lamped tables and flexible armchairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Geisel Library’s main-level Reference area has large tables with lamps and soft armchairs with attached swivel tables.
cards.access_notes: Located on Geisel Library’s main level, where quiet talking is allowed. The Reference Desk is also on this level.

cards.entity_name: Geisel Library Main-Level Book Stacks Seating
cards.title: Geisel Library Main-Level Book Stacks Seating
cards.subtitle: Main Level · carrels and a window-side table
cards.notes: Use the individual carrels for focused reading, or claim the table by the window when you need room to keep books and a laptop open.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels and a table set between the main-level stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Geisel Library’s main-level book-stack seating includes individual study carrels and a large table by a window between the stacks.
cards.access_notes: Located on Geisel Library’s main level, where quiet talking is allowed. Follow library sound-level and food policies.

cards.title: Geisel Library Upper-Level Mixed Seating
cards.subtitle: Upper Level · soft chairs, carrels, and a window table
cards.notes: Head upstairs for silent study; choose the soft seating, a carrel, or the large window table based on how much material you need nearby.
cards.short_summary: A silent upper-level mix of soft chairs, carrels, and window seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Geisel Library’s upper-level mixed seating includes soft chairs, individual study carrels, and a large table by a window; the upper level is designated for silent study.
cards.access_notes: Located on Geisel Library’s silent-study upper level. The group study rooms are not sound-proof, so keep noise low throughout the floor.

cards.entity_name: Geisel Library Upper-Level Individual Study Carrels
cards.title: Geisel Library Upper-Level Individual Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Upper Level · silent individual seating
cards.notes: Bring a focused solo task to these upper-level carrels, where the library designates the floor for silent study and mostly individual seating.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated upper-level individual seating in a silent-study area.
cards.evidence_claim: The upper level of Geisel Library is a silent-study floor with mostly individual study carrels, plus some window seating and dimmer lighting.
cards.access_notes: Located on Geisel Library’s upper level; maintain silent-study expectations. Follow library food and beverage policies.

cards.entity_name: Geisel Library Lower-Level Group Study Area
cards.title: Geisel Library Lower-Level Group Study Area
cards.subtitle: Lower Level · alternative collaborative seating
cards.notes: Use this floor for a conversation-based assignment when reservable rooms are occupied, and keep discussion at the library’s normal-volume expectation.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level alternative for group work when rooms are occupied.
cards.evidence_claim: Geisel Library identifies the lower level as an alternative group study space when group rooms are in use, with normal-volume conversations allowed.
cards.access_notes: Located on Geisel Library’s lower level. Normal-volume conversations are allowed; louder conversations may be asked to lower their volume.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Manchester destinations on corridors within the practical driving orbit of Saint Anselm College.

cards.title: Nature trail at Blodget Park
cards.subtitle: Front Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Front Street to reach the park’s nature trail and fishing area. Bring footwear suited to an unpaved outdoor walk and leave time to explore the brookside setting.
cards.short_summary: A city-managed conservation park with a trail and fishing amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester Parks and Recreation lists Blodget Park / Black Brook on Front Street and identifies a nature trail and fishing as amenities.
cards.source_title: Blodget Park - Black Brook | City of Manchester
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; check conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Dorrs Pond at Livingston Park
cards.subtitle: Daniel Webster Highway / Hooksett Road corridor
cards.notes: Head up the Daniel Webster Highway corridor for Livingston Park and its Dorrs Pond facilities. Use the city’s park information to plan around the outdoor amenities available there.
cards.short_summary: A named city park associated with Dorrs Pond and a park bath house.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Manchester lists the Dorrs Pond Skate House and Livingston Bath House at Livingston Park on Daniel Webster Highway North.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park facilities; seasonal operations may vary.

cards.title: Fields and playground at Stevens Park
cards.subtitle: Mammoth Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow Mammoth Road toward Stevens Park for a stop centered on its sports fields and playground. Check the city’s current field schedule if you intend to use programmed facilities.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood park documented with athletic fields and a playground.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester’s parks master plan describes Stevens Park as a sports park with a playground and identifies an entrance at Mammoth Road.
cards.source_title: Greening the City: Manchester Parks and Recreation Master Plan
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park; availability of fields can vary with scheduled use.

cards.title: Golf course on Mammoth Road
cards.subtitle: Mammoth Road corridor
cards.notes: Use Mammoth Road to find the Derryfield golf course. If you want to play, consult the club directly for current tee-time, course-access, and event details before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A named Manchester golf-course destination on Mammoth Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Manchester lists Derryfield Country Club at 625 Mammoth Road.
cards.access_notes: Golf and event access may require advance arrangements or payment.

cards.title: Currier collections on Ash Street
cards.subtitle: Ash Street corridor
cards.notes: Take Ash Street to the Currier Museum of Art for its collection galleries and exhibition program. Review the museum’s visitor information for current exhibitions and entry details.
cards.short_summary: Manchester’s art museum, documented by the city’s museum network.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester Museums identifies the Currier Museum of Art as a Manchester museum destination.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and hours should be confirmed with the museum before visiting.

cards.title: Research stop on Pine Street
cards.subtitle: Pine Street corridor
cards.notes: Make Pine Street your route to Manchester City Library when you need a public research or reading stop. Check the library calendar and service information before planning a longer visit.
cards.short_summary: A named public library destination in Manchester’s central area.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Manchester lists Carpenter Library at 405 Pine Street among its library buildings.
cards.access_notes: Library services and room access may vary by schedule.

cards.title: Open space on Elm Street
cards.subtitle: Elm Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Elm Street to reach Veterans Memorial Park between Central and Merrimack streets. It works as a quick outdoor pause while visiting nearby downtown cultural destinations.
cards.short_summary: A named city park positioned on the central Elm Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester Parks and Recreation states that Veterans Memorial Park is on Elm Street between Central and Merrimack streets.
cards.source_title: Veterans Memorial Park | City of Manchester
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; city permitting rules apply to organized events.

cards.title: Murals just off Elm Street
cards.subtitle: Elm Street corridor, between 836 and 844 Elm Street
cards.notes: Walk the Elm Street corridor to Cat Alley and photograph the painted-brick mural sequence. Enter from the block between The Bookery at 844 Elm and 836 Elm Street.
cards.short_summary: A public pedestrian alley with more than 20 cat-themed murals.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Manchester says Cat Alley has more than 20 murals between The Bookery at 844 Elm Street and 836 Elm Street and is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian walkway; be considerate of adjacent businesses and pedestrians.

cards.title: Manchester history in the Millyard
cards.subtitle: Commercial Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Commercial Street to approach the Millyard Museum and learn about Manchester’s industrial history. Pair the visit with time to look at the surrounding historic mill district from public areas.
cards.short_summary: A museum in Mill No. 3 focused on Manchester history.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Manchester states that the Millyard Museum is housed in Mill No. 3 and tells Manchester’s story from its earliest inhabitants to the present.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and exhibit access should be confirmed before travel.

cards.title: Hands-on science in the Millyard
cards.subtitle: Bedford Street corridor
cards.notes: Take Bedford Street into the Millyard for hands-on science exhibits at SEE Science Center. Review the center’s visitor details and any timed programming before choosing a visit date.
cards.short_summary: A Manchester science destination with interactive exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Manchester describes SEE Science Center as providing a hands-on interactive scientific experience for children and families.
cards.access_notes: Exhibit entry may require admission; verify current visitor information.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Saint Anselm traditions spanning the Hilltop’s academic, seasonal, service, nursing, and literary life.

cards.title: See Your Class Banner in Davison
cards.subtitle: Davison Hall · a Saint Anselm class-year marker
cards.notes: Find your class banner in Davison Hall, then return during commencement week to see this long-running class-year marker reach its final chapter.
cards.short_summary: Each class’s banner hangs in Davison Hall until commencement week.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm identifies the hanging of class banners in Davison Hall until commencement week as one of its favorite traditions.
cards.access_notes: Davison Hall access follows current campus building policies.

cards.title: Enter the Gingerbread House Competition
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · annual holiday tradition
cards.notes: Form a team and watch for the seasonal entry announcement; plan your design around the contest’s current rules, deadline, and display arrangements.
cards.short_summary: An annual student competition turns gingerbread construction into a Hilltop holiday ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm lists entering the annual Gingerbread House Competition among its favorite campus traditions.
cards.access_notes: Offered seasonally; confirm current entry details through campus announcements.

cards.title: Take Part in Relay For Life
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · annual fundraising tradition
cards.notes: Join or support a registered team through the current campus Relay For Life effort, and use the official event information for participation details.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus fundraiser links student participation with the American Cancer Society’s Relay For Life.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm describes Relay For Life as a tradition through which participants raise more than $100,000 annually.
cards.access_notes: Registration and fundraising expectations depend on the current event.

cards.title: Share the Christmas Feast
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · seasonal dining tradition
cards.notes: Check the end-of-semester dining calendar and attend with friends when the feast is scheduled; dining access and menu details are announced each year.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal communal meal brings students together as the fall term closes.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm names dining with friends during the Christmas Feast as a favorite campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal event; confirm date, venue, and dining eligibility in current announcements.

cards.title: Read a Sonnet for Shakespeare
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · annual April reading
cards.notes: Volunteer for a reading slot or stop by the celebration to hear sonnets and performances; consult the English Department’s current event notice.
cards.short_summary: Saint Anselm marks Shakespeare’s birthday with a campus reading of all 154 sonnets.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm documents an annual Shakespeare’s Birthday Celebration that grew from a 1989 reading of all 154 sonnets.
cards.source_title: Annual Shakespeare's Birthday Celebration | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Held around Shakespeare’s birthday; reader sign-up and format vary by year.

cards.title: Witness the Blessing of the Hands
cards.subtitle: Abbey Church · undergraduate nursing tradition
cards.notes: Nursing students and their guests can follow the annual ceremony notice, which honors sophomores as they prepare to begin their first clinicals.
cards.short_summary: Professors bless sophomore nursing students’ hands before their first clinical experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm calls the Blessing of the Hands a beloved undergraduate nursing tradition held in the Abbey Church.
cards.source_title: 2026 Blessing of the Hands | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: The 2026 ceremony welcomed friends and family; verify future ceremony details with Nursing.

cards.title: Celebrate at Nurse Pinning
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · nursing milestone
cards.notes: For eligible nursing students and invited guests, follow the Jean School’s commencement-season communications for the ceremony’s current date and format.
cards.short_summary: A nursing-program ceremony recognizes graduates as they enter the profession.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm lists Nurse Pinning among the additional opportunities and traditions available to its nursing students.
cards.access_notes: Intended for nursing graduates and their invited guests; event arrangements vary annually.

cards.title: Start With Brian Maguire Day of Service
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation · Saint Anselm College
cards.notes: New students should follow orientation assignments and service-site instructions for this annual opening-week opportunity to work with community partners.
cards.short_summary: New students begin their Anselmian experience with a coordinated day of service.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm states that its annual Brian Maguire Day of Service is part of new-student orientation.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: For new students; service locations, transportation, and requirements are provided during orientation.

cards.title: Look for the Holiday Fair
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · seasonal campus tradition
cards.notes: Watch Student Affairs and campus-event listings for the current fair date, location, vendors, and any participation details before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal campus event named among the college’s longstanding traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm includes Holiday Fair in its published list of college traditions.
cards.access_notes: Offered seasonally; confirm whether the event is open to visitors and any current requirements.

cards.title: Join New Student Orientation
cards.subtitle: Saint Anselm College · first-year welcome tradition
cards.notes: Complete the required orientation schedule, including academic and Anselmian-life sessions, and use official communications for move-in and program details.
cards.short_summary: The annual welcome program introduces incoming students to Saint Anselm’s academic and community life.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm includes Freshman Orientation among its traditions and publishes annual new-student orientation programming.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Designed for incoming students and their families; dates and required sessions are published annually.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Saint Anselm College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A first-weekend campus sequence built around named Saint Anselm destinations for gathering, eating, exploring, studying, arts, recreation, and reflection.

cards.title: Start with campus history
cards.subtitle: Alumni Hall · first stop
cards.notes: Begin outside the college’s first campus building, then use the stop to orient yourself before moving into the central academic and residential areas.
cards.short_summary: A historic starting point for getting your bearings on the Hilltop.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm identifies Alumni Hall as the first building on campus; it now contains offices, classrooms, the Chapel Art Center, and student housing.
cards.access_notes: The official tour describes current uses; follow posted access guidance for interior areas.

cards.title: Meet up on the Green
cards.subtitle: Campus Green · early afternoon
cards.notes: Choose the Campus Green as an easy outdoor meeting point, then make a plan with new classmates for the next few stops on your weekend loop.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor gathering point used in the college’s new-student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm’s 2026 new-student orientation schedule lists a new-student BBQ and a reflection session on the Campus Green.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access and programming vary with weather and the college calendar.

cards.title: Pause for a meal
cards.subtitle: Davison Dining Hall · lunch or dinner
cards.notes: Bring your student ID and use a meal break to compare schedules, find dietary labels, and set a low-key plan for the evening with your group.
cards.short_summary: The college’s main dining facility and a practical regrouping stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm calls Davison Dining Hall its main campus dining facility and says student IDs are needed to buy food at campus dining facilities.
cards.source_title: Dining on Campus | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Food purchase requires a Saint Anselm student ID; check Dining Services for current service details.

cards.entity_name: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center
cards.title: Find the student hub
cards.subtitle: Jean Student Center · afternoon
cards.notes: Walk through the center, note the student-service offices, and take a few minutes in a lounge or study area before choosing your next activity.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building for services, gathering, study, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The college describes the Jean Student Center as a hub with student services, lounge and study areas, an auditorium, café, bookstore, and event space.
cards.source_title: Roger and Francine Jean Student Center | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Some rooms and event spaces may be reserved; use the building’s posted guidance.

cards.title: Set up a study reset
cards.subtitle: Geisel Library · late afternoon
cards.notes: Locate the circulation and reference desks, then reserve a study room if needed so you have a calm place ready for coursework after the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A study-and-research stop with reservable rooms and librarian help.
cards.evidence_claim: Geisel Library offers study spaces, research help, and study-room reservations through its Circulation Desk.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are reserved through the Circulation Desk; consult the library’s current hours.

cards.entity_name: Alva de Mars Megan Chapel Art Center
cards.title: Look at the current exhibition
cards.subtitle: Chapel Art Center · early evening
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition or cultural-events information, then take a quiet pass through the collection before heading to a performance or game.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery in a former chapel with exhibitions and cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm says the Chapel Art Center, formerly a chapel, houses the college’s permanent collection and presents exhibitions and cultural events.
cards.source_title: The Arts at Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions and events vary during the academic year; confirm current gallery availability before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Dana Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Check the performance calendar
cards.subtitle: Dana Center · evening option
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled show, lecture, or student-theatre production, and confirm the event’s admission and seating details before making it your evening plan.
cards.short_summary: A performing-arts venue with recurring lectures and productions.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm says dozens of performances and lectures are presented annually in the Dana Center’s Koonz Theatre, home to the Anselmian Abbey Players.
cards.access_notes: Events, tickets, and admission conditions vary; verify the individual listing.

cards.title: Catch a Hawks contest
cards.subtitle: Grappone Stadium · evening option
cards.notes: If a home contest is scheduled, meet your group at the stadium and check the event listing for start time, entry instructions, and spectator information.
cards.short_summary: A named campus stadium and turf field for Saint Anselm athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm lists Grappone Stadium as a 2,500-seat stadium with a turf field among its athletic facilities.
cards.access_notes: Home schedules and spectator entry conditions change by event; consult Athletics before going.

cards.title: Learn the recreation layout
cards.subtitle: Carr Center · active break
cards.notes: Take an active break by locating the gym and fitness areas, then review current eligibility and facility rules before planning a future workout or intramural visit.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose athletics building with fitness, court, and team spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm describes the Carr Center as a multipurpose facility with basketball, volleyball, racquetball, tennis courts, and a fitness center.
cards.access_notes: The college says the Carr Center and Spagnuolo Fitness Center serve the Saint Anselm population; verify current facility rules.

cards.title: Close with a quiet visit
cards.subtitle: Abbey Church · reflection stop
cards.notes: End the loop with a quiet visit or attend a listed service if it fits your beliefs and schedule; check the current schedule before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A campus place for prayer and reflection with recurring services.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Anselm identifies the Abbey Church as a place for prayer and reflection and publishes daily prayer and Eucharist schedules there.
cards.source_title: Mass & Prayer Schedule | Saint Anselm College
cards.access_notes: Services follow separate in-session and recess schedules; consult the current college schedule and posted church updates.
